filter: Extract ECG identifier from text; join fold; skip folds9/10 before json.loads or any nonidentifier annotation access

interpretation.wave_coordinates: All 4,854 wave questions contain one selected answer: 4,813 valid numeric time intervals and 41 recognizable QRS-ordinal intervals. The latter are valid symbolic spans. The frozen invalid_selected_time_ranges counter records a timestamp-parser coverage limitation, not 41 clinically invalid labels.
interpretation.lead_question: Every V5-versus-V6 question asks which lead shows the larger R amplitude. All occur within the LVH criterion combining S amplitude in V1 with R amplitude in V5/V6 above 3.5 mV. The lead-question text itself does not specify a current beat or assert that the selected lead is diseased.
interpretation.shortcut_scope: The 64.3137% option-zero result is dominated by 144/168 answers favoring V5 within the fixed [V5,V6] options. For the other 87 single-answer lead questions, option zero is correct 20/87=22.99%, versus uniform 20%. This is signal-free predictability from an imbalanced answer content plus fixed ordering; it does not establish randomization corruption, incorrect labels, broad localization competence, or exploitation by a published model.
interpretation.report_wording: Stored-order lead answers showed a narrow content/position imbalance driven by V5-versus-V6 R-amplitude comparisons. This does not validate clinical lead localization. Shuffling option order would remove a positional shortcut but would not remove the always-choose-V5 content prior.
interpretation.nonclinical: No waveform, diagnosis predictor, neural model, or original No Time To Train inference was run. Verification is confined to safe folds1–8 annotation structure and all-fold identifier counts.
